claims.text: The UK announced a three-year Be Ready campaign on 22 October, advising households to prepare for three days of ordinary service disruption, including severe weather. The government says much of the advice has existed since 2024. This is not an announcement that war is imminent.

The European Commission's statement on the attempted Leipzig-Halle cargo-plane attack was dated 2 September, not a new October warning. It relayed the German government's attribution to Russia and called for infrastructure resilience.

NATO's Secretary General acknowledged hybrid attacks but said on 14 October that the alliance saw no imminent threat against NATO territory. This is an assessment at that date, not a guarantee about future events.

Gulf maritime danger is not imaginary: the US maritime advisory describes continued threats and attacks on commercial vessels. The IEA's 14 October report says crude flows had partly recovered while tanker attacks, freight costs and constrained refined products kept the recovery fragile. scenarios.trigger: Disclosed higher replacement costs, customer pass-through or weaker demand; confirm with current prices and breadth.
scenarios.invalidation: Stable realised procurement costs, maintained company margins and stronger broad participation.
scenarios.horizon: Next corporate updates and next one to three sessions; no probability or price target assigned.

watchpoints.signal: 27 October SGX closing read after trade-at-close: verify fresh STI, bank contribution, breadth, turnover, FX/rates and each sector. Do not substitute this recovery for the closing report.
watchpoints.confirms: Broad participation and stable energy operations support the contained-disruption case.
watchpoints.contradicts: Weak breadth plus verified operational or margin stress contradict it.

watchpoints.signal: Verify actual KORE release separately from its timetable; check Digital Core REIT after-hours update, publication timestamp and financing/occupancy commentary when available.
watchpoints.confirms: Maintained cash generation, occupancy and funding access support property resilience.
watchpoints.contradicts: Weak leasing or higher funding costs undercut it; no release means an unresolved data gap, not a negative result.

exchanges.name: SGX cash securities — regular calendar verified; live venue/individual halt status not independently established

sentiment.assessment: Previous-close neutral participation with soft index leadership; current-session sentiment DATA INCOMPLETE.
sentiment.indicators: 26 October: 252 advances / 252 declines, S$1.4bn turnover, STI -0.1%, all three local banks lower. These are dated observable proxies, not a survey or current opening indication. Current volatility, flows and political-post sentiment were not verified.

sectors.finding: September electronics output +5.7% y/y and precision engineering +31% in the secondary EDB account; neither is a technology-share return.
sectors.implication: Manufacturing demand remains uneven; equipment exposure differs from domestic-facing firms.
sectors.watchpoint: Verify orders, customer concentration, FX and current technology-stock breadth.

sectors.finding: 26 October Singtel indexed release: Nxera and Sembcorp signed an exploratory low-carbon-power MOU. Direct body was not rendered; no current telco share performance verified.
sectors.implication: Potential power access supports data-centre expansion only if projects, permits and economics become binding.
sectors.watchpoint: Check definitive supply contracts, commissioning dates and capital obligations; do not book MOU revenue.

sectors.finding: No verified 27 October retailer, travel or hospitality opening evidence. MAS 14 October context noted weakness in consumer-facing activity.
sectors.implication: Higher input costs may pressure demand, but tourism, currency and company mix can offset; no sector direction assigned.
sectors.watchpoint: Refresh issuer sales and bookings, current breadth and any energy-cost pass-through.

sectors.finding: No verified current staples basket or margin release. MAS historical outlook highlighted food-cost risks.
sectors.implication: Defensive demand does not guarantee defensive margins when inputs rise.
sectors.watchpoint: Check realised commodity costs, hedges and pricing against volumes.

sectors.finding: 25 October official gas statement confirms reduced supply with replacement available; no verified current oil, LNG or energy-equity prices.
sectors.implication: Supply continuity lowers immediate shortage concerns; procurement cost and contractual recovery remain distinct unknowns.
sectors.watchpoint: Verify replacement costs and issuer disclosures before inferring earnings effects.

sectors.finding: 26 October DBS, OCBC and UOB fell 0.3%, 0.2% and 0.7%. No reliable 27 October bank/opening quotes or fresh funding curve retrieved.
sectors.implication: Heavyweight weakness can explain index softness without proving systemic stress.
sectors.watchpoint: Refresh bank participation, funding costs, credit-loss disclosures and current index contribution.

sectors.finding: September biomedical production fell 32.8% y/y in the EDB secondary account, partly reflecting pharmaceutical product mix; this is not hospital-sector revenue.
sectors.implication: Production mix and softer medical-technology exports require different explanations; neither proves healthcare share weakness.
sectors.watchpoint: Seek primary EDB release and issuer segment data before generalising.

sectors.finding: September transport engineering output +10.6% y/y in the secondary EDB account; the 26 October energy lecture outlined grid expansion.
sectors.implication: Potential infrastructure demand is longer term; tenders, contract awards and margins matter before revenue recognition.
sectors.watchpoint: Check funded awards, backlog conversion and energy exposure; no current sector prices verified.

sectors.finding: September chemicals output -4.6% y/y in the secondary EDB account, with softer demand and feedstock constraints discussed.
sectors.implication: Feedstock and demand exposures vary across listed businesses; this is not a materials-index return.
sectors.watchpoint: Verify company-specific feedstock cover and selling spreads, plus fresh basket prices.

sectors.finding: 23 October official statistics showed Q3 private-home, office and retail price indices rising 1.4%, 0.8% and 1.1% q/q; these are property prices, not rents or REIT returns. KORE and Digital Core release calendars need outcome checks.
sectors.implication: Asset-value resilience may coexist with funding and leasing pressure. US-property REIT exposure differs from Singapore property.
sectors.watchpoint: Read actual results, debt maturity, occupancy and cash distribution coverage; refresh sector prices.

sectors.finding: Official gas cover and 26 October grid expansion plans provide physical-system context. No current generator margin, tariff surprise or utility basket return verified.
sectors.implication: Reliability investment can add opportunity and capital needs simultaneously; adequate fuel does not fix its cost.
sectors.watchpoint: Verify procurement, regulatory recovery and funded projects rather than equating plans with profits.

spillovers.scenario: Conditional: regional fuel substitution and infrastructure sourcing can affect ASEAN energy trade; Singapore manufacturing evidence may inform, but does not establish, Asian technology demand.
spillovers.trigger: Regional supplier disclosures and export/order data corroborate the transmission.
spillovers.invalidation: Contract cover and country-specific demand keep effects local; basket calendars and current prices remain separate checks.

spillovers.scenario: Conditional: grid and power investment could create demand for European equipment suppliers, while fuel competition could affect costs.
spillovers.trigger: Verified supplier awards or cargo/pricing evidence; a Singapore plan alone is insufficient.
spillovers.invalidation: Projects remain preliminary, suppliers differ or no price transmission appears.

spillovers.scenario: Conditional: Singapore data-centre energy planning matters to AI infrastructure capacity; US-property REIT releases can inform local asset-specific funding risk.
spillovers.trigger: Binding power capacity and actual REIT operational updates, not MOU headlines or release calendars.
spillovers.invalidation: Delayed capacity or improving financing contradicts a simple positive/negative spillover; no US opening call is made.
